subject: Escalation liaison matrix & data-transfer obligations (AtlasWorks DPA)
messages:

Cc: security@atlasworks.com
Date: 2026-10-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Incident notification: liaison points & cross-border transfer obligations

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. As we get closer to finalizing the DPA addendum, Legal at AtlasWorks asked us to document the operational notification process specifically around:
- point-of-contact (liaison) for security/forensics;
- evidence/handover windows for preserved data;
- permitted cross-border transfers to subprocessors and any country-specific notices; and
- pragmatic timelines for notification and acknowledgement (we need a ‘hard’ SLA for initial notification plus expected follow-up cadence).

Can you share Redwood’s internal liaison matrix and proposed clause language for timelines (e.g., initial notification within X hours, follow-up within Y business days)? Also attaching a short template our procurement team prefers for the addendum.

Appreciate a response by EOD Wednesday so we can keep the procurement review on track.

Best,
Katie
Head of Security Operations
AtlasWorks

Attachments: atlas-dpa-template.pdf (referenced)

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.example.com>
To: Katie Lewis <katie.lewis@atlasworks.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.example.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.example.com
Date: 2026-10-12T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Incident notification: liaison points & cross-border transfer obligations

Katie —

Thanks for the clear asks. High level summary and next steps below:

1) Liaison matrix: we maintain a tiered contact list (security ops, legal, engineering) with 24/7 pager escalation for incidents that meet your "security incident" threshold. I can attach an anonymized matrix but will remove internal phone numbers.

2) Evidence & handover windows: Redwood can commit to preserving relevant logs and KV cache dumps for 90 days for the purposes of an investigation; evidence handover (redacted where necessary) can be initiated within 5 business days of receiving a formal request and appropriate legal authorization (e.g., DPA appendix or subpoena). For EU-personal-data-specific requests we follow the cross-border control playbook — see proposed clause below.

3) Notification timelines: proposed operational SLOs — initial notification within 24 hours of detection (if feasible), a triage update within 72 hours, and a detailed incident report within 15 business days. If customer-facing impact is large we trigger an expedited cadence (initial: 12 hours). We can surface stronger timelines for AtlasWorks in an addendum.

4) Cross-border transfers and subprocessors: Redwood uses a subprocessor list with advance notice. For transfers where export/import controls or local law require notice we will: (a) notify AtlasWorks within 48 hours of confirming the necessity of transfer, and (b) provide mitigation controls (encryption, minimized dataset, pseudonymization) where applicable.

I've looped in Marissa from Legal to propose DPA language and Neha from Privacy to confirm evidence retention commitments.

Next actions: Marissa will send proposed addendum language and an escalation matrix XLSX. After you review we'll route for DocuSign.

—Ben
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: incident-liaison-matrix.xlsx (anonymized contact roles)

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>
To: Katie Lewis <katie.lewis@atlasworks.com>, ben_carter@redwood.example.com
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.example.com
Date: 2026-10-13T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed clause language + redline (AtlasWorks DPA addendum)

Katie —

Following up with suggested legal language for the addendum. Major points emphasized in the redline:

• Notification & acknowledgement. Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to provide initial written notice of a Confirmed Security Incident to the AtlasWorks security contact within twenty-four (24) hours of confirmation. Such notice will include a summary of the incident, affected data categories, and immediate mitigation steps. Redwood will provide subsequent status updates as information becomes available and a final report no later than fifteen (15) business days after confirmation, subject to reasonable extensions where forensic or law-enforcement constraints apply.

• Evidence preservation & transfer. Redwood will preserve relevant logs and artifacts for a minimum of ninety (90) days. Evidence transfers shall be made following AtlasWorks' written request and subject to agreed redaction and export controls; Redwood will initiate a handover within five (5) business days of receipt of a legally valid request.

• Subprocessors & cross-border transfers. Redwood will provide a current subprocessor list and notify AtlasWorks at least thirty (30) days in advance of adding a subprocessor that will process AtlasWorks personal data. For urgent operational reasons where a subprocessor must be engaged sooner, Redwood will notify AtlasWorks within forty-eight (48) hours and provide mitigations. Transfers outside the European Economic Area will rely on Standard Contractual Clauses (or equivalent) and any additional safeguards requested by AtlasWorks, where technically feasible.

• Escalation liaison matrix. Attached is an operational matrix (incident-liaison-matrix.xlsx). The matrix maps Redwood roles to AtlasWorks contacts and expected response SLAs.

Please see the attached redline (DPA-addendum-AtlasWorks-redline.docx). We're flexible on tightening the SLA numbers for AtlasWorks; we understand procurement prefers discrete hours instead of business days for early notification steps — we can adopt that in the final addendum.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: DPA-addendum-AtlasWorks-redline.docx; scope-diagram.png

From: Katie Lewis <katie.lewis@atlasworks.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.example.com, ben_carter@redwood.example.com
Date: 2026-10-14T10:41:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed clause language + redline (AtlasWorks DPA addendum)

Marissa —

Thanks for the thorough redline. A few points from AtlasWorks Legal & Security:

1) Initial notification: we'd prefer an initial notification within 12 hours for incidents classified as customer-impacting (availability or confirmed exfiltration).
2) Evidence handover: the 5 business day initiation is acceptable provided Redwood can flag critical logs (auth, access, audit) for expedited transfer within 48 hours if requested.
3) Subprocessor notice: 30 days is standard; however we require a written mitigation plan for any subprocessor added with less than 30 days' notice.

We also need to capture a short-statement escalation path to AtlasWorks' Head of Security for incidents that meet our "critical" threshold — would you include that in the matrix?

If you can update the redline with the 12-hour initial-notify option and the expedited-log-transfer note, procurement can route the final addendum. We also prefer DocuSign for execution.

Best,
Katie
